Secondly, the uncertainty of Δ<sub>m</sub> has to be calculated:

$$u_\Delta = \sqrt{u_m^2 + u_{CRM}^2}$$

u<sub>Δ</sub> ………combined uncertainty of the measured value and the certified value

u<sub>m</sub>………uncertainty of the measured value

u<sub>CRM</sub>……uncertainty of the certified value

The uncertainty of the certified value is calculated by dividing the expanded uncertainty U, shown at the certificate, by the factor k = 2.

The uncertainty of the measured value can be expressed approximately by use of the reproducibility standard deviation which was determined by the interlaboratory comparison for the certification (for data base cp. attachment 3 of the certification report BAM-D001):

d<sub>10</sub>-value: u<sub>m</sub> = 0.4 µm

d<sub>50</sub>-value: u<sub>m</sub> = 0.28 µm

d<sub>90</sub>-value: u<sub>m</sub> = 1.7 µm

The calculated combined uncertainty has to be multiplied by the factor k = 2. The result correlates to a confidence level of approx. 95 %.

$$U_\Delta = 2 \times u_\Delta$$

In a final step Δ<sub>m</sub> has to be compared with U<sub>Δ</sub> to evaluate the performance of the measurement. There is no significant difference between the measured value and the certified value if Δ<sub>m</sub> ≤ U<sub>Δ</sub>.

The material has to be stored in a dry atmosphere.
